title: Is the TI LP-AM243 the right board for my project?
short: A LaunchPad development kit for TI's AM2434, a chip with four 800 MHz Cortex-R5F real-time cores, one Cortex-M4F and two PRU-ICSSG programmable real-time units. CoreMark is 2,931 per second on one core and 11,730 on all four at once. Of 194 SDK example projects for the board, 163 build from a Mac terminal, and of the 121 first-core projects loaded, 82 printed a pass. Upstream Zephyr's hello_world and blinky run on the first core. The Ethernet example linked at 1 Gb but never got an address from the house network, so no network number was measured.

meet.what: A LaunchPad development kit for TI's AM2434 industrial MCU, with an XDS110 debug probe on the board. The board needs its own 5 V, 3 A USB-C charger on J10 and a micro-B cable on J20 for the probe and the console. A load into RAM leaves the 64 MB flash and the boot switches as shipped.
facts: 4 Arm Cortex-R5F at 800 MHz and 1 Cortex-M4F; 2 PRU-ICSSG units (PRU clock 200 MHz)
2 MB on-chip OCSRAM; 64 kB TCM per R5F core in dual-core mode; no DDR on this package
64 MB quad SPI on the board
XDS110 on micro-B J20, firmware 3.0.0.15; the console is the Application/User UART at 115200
USB-C J10 must advertise 3 A on its CC pins; a red LD9 means it did not
MCU+ SDK for AM243x 12.01.00.33, CCStudio 21.0.1, TI Arm Clang 4.0.4.LTS, SysConfig 1.27.0, Zephyr 4.5.0-rc2

projects.t: Run a program from RAM with the switches as shipped
projects.result: About 4 s from the command to a running single-core image, with flash and boot switches untouched. A power cycle returns the board to the firmware in its flash

projects.t: Blink an LED, edit the period, prove the rate
projects.result: 31 s from the command to 16 verified pin edges 250 ms apart, scripted, board already powered and surveyed; the steps themselves take 13 s
2,931 per second on one core (3.664 per MHz, TCM), 2,926 to 2,928 on each of the other three, 11,730 on all four at once. TI's page lists 3,015.63. TI Arm Clang 5.1.1 gives 3,151

projects.t: TI's SDK examples, built and run from a terminal
projects.result: 163 of 194 projects build; of 121 first-core projects loaded into RAM, 82 printed a pass, 2 a failure, 30 output with no verdict and 7 nothing in 30 s
3.19 us round trip per partner with four partners, 2.08 with three, 1.61 with one, 400,000 trips per run. The example hangs on a second start unless the chip is reset and given 12 s first

projects.t: A PRU core writing a pin register
projects.result: A write takes 1 cycle unrolled (5.3 ns) and 2 cycles in a loop (10 ns) by the PRU's own counter. The pad was not routed, so no scope has seen the rate
Upstream lp_am243/am2434/r5f0_0 hello_world and blinky run from RAM. The M4 hello_world builds but was not run; the M4 blinky does not build because the board file has no led0 alias
One port linked at 1 Gb full duplex, but DHCP gave no lease in 130 s and no throughput or latency number was measured. The example's UP message comes from lwIP, not the PHY

chains.t: TI's SDK and compiler, from a Mac terminal
chains.why: There is no Mac installer for the SDK: run TI's Linux installer in an amd64 container and copy the folder. Then the SDK makefiles, SysConfig and TI Arm Clang build from the terminal, and am243x/prebuild.sh builds 15 examples

chains.t: A Linux demo on the chip
chains.why: The chip is a microcontroller with no Linux port. The chip's fast software-toggled pin work belongs on a PRU core

chains.t: A radio or wireless demo on the chip
chains.why: The chip has no radio. Radio demos need a separate radio board

combine_title: What else we tried, and how it went
combine_lede: Each row is something we tried beyond the standard list. A row that did not work is recorded with its reason, not left out.

Of 121 first-core projects loaded, 82 printed a pass

good_for: Real-time control that wants four 800 MHz cores and PRU cores on one chip
Comparing an Arm real-time core with the AM263P on the same code
Running and benchmarking from RAM on a Mac without touching the flash
Trying upstream Zephyr on an R5F core
not_for: Anything with a radio or Linux: the chip has neither
Projects that need an Ethernet number: none was measured
Projects that need a scope-confirmed PRU pin rate: none was seen
Power or energy numbers: none were measured
buy: Sold by TI as the LP-AM243 LaunchPad development kit. It needs a separate 5 V, 3 A USB-C charger and a micro-B cable; the probe is on the board.
gotchas: DSLite lists the cores but every connect fails with error -1170 at CS_DAP_0 and a red LED is on
Give the board a 3 A USB-C charger, then replug the micro-B. **Tag: Setup or handling.**
TI's ipc_notify_echo hangs on its second start

Set AM243X_BARE=1 and load from RAM. **Tag: Setup or handling.**
The lwIP example says UP for both ports but nothing answers
The line comes from lwIP, not the PHY: print each PHY's link state and check the far end of the cable goes to a switch or mesh node. **Tag: TI example default.**
measured_on: Measured 2026-11-05 to 2026-11-08 on an Intel Mac with CCStudio 21.0.1, MCU+ SDK for AM243x 12.01.00.33, TI Arm Clang 4.0.4.LTS, SysConfig 1.27.0 and Zephyr 4.5.0-rc2. R5F cores at 800 MHz.

next.title: What do I do first with the LP-AM243?
steps: Plug the 5 V, 3 A USB-C charger into J10, then the micro-B cable into J20. LD9 stays dark.
Run am243x/prebuild.sh to build 15 SDK examples.
Run an image from RAM: python3 am243x/tools/ram_capture.py <image.out> run.log --until "All tests have passed".
Read the FAQ before your first multi-core example.

line: Four 800 MHz real-time cores and two PRU cores, run from RAM on a Mac.
